reviews.notes: Accurately represents Krishna's opening address to Arjuna promising supreme words of welfare; footnote marker anomaly [FN#l6] accurately anchored.
Directly matches that neither gods nor great rishis know the Lord's primal origin, for He is the source of all.
Faithfully renders knowing Krishna as unborn, unbegun (anādi), and sovereign Lord of the worlds, freeing mortals from all sin.
Shared two-verse span with 10.5 verified; Arnold combines and interweaves the psychic dispositions and qualities of 10.4-10.5 into a single rhyming catalog.
Shared two-verse span with 10.4 verified; correctly links the integrated poetic passage enumerating the diverse natures proceeding from the Lord alone.
Faithfully represents the Seven Great Sages, Ancient Four, and Manus born of Krishna's mind, progenitors of mankind.
Matches knowing in truth this divine vibhūti and yoga, attaining unwavering steadfast communion.
Accurately renders the opening of the Caturślokī Gītā: Krishna as source of all from whom all evolves, worshipped by the wise with devotion.
Directly corresponds to maccittā madgataprāṇā bodhayantaḥ parasparam, devotees rejoicing and finding peace in mutual contemplation.
Faithfully conveys the granting of buddhiyoga (understanding) to constant devotees that they may come to Him.
Accurately represents the Lord dwelling within out of compassion to dispel darkness of ignorance with the lamp of wisdom.
Directly matches Arjuna's eulogy addressing Krishna as Parabrahm, supreme abode, supreme purifier, eternal divine Person, and unborn Lord.
Accurately cites the testimony of all sages (Narada, Asita, Devala, Vyasa) and Krishna's own direct self-revelation.
Renders Arjuna holding all Krishna's words as truth, and that neither devas nor danavas (demons) grasp His divine manifestation.
Faithfully captures that only the Lord Himself knows Himself, calling Him Creator of beings, God of gods, and King of the Universe.
Matches Arjuna's plea to hear without reserve the divine perfections (vibhūtis) whereby the Lord pervades all worlds.
Accurately represents asking how the yogi may continually meditate on and know the Lord across His multiple aspects.
Faithfully renders the request for elaborate description of yoga and vibhūti, declaring no satiety in drinking such nectar (Amrit [FN#18]).
Directly matches Krishna consenting ('Hanta! So be it!') to declare prominent aspects of His boundless manifestations.
Captures the foundational declaration: Krishna is the Self seated in every heart, the beginning, middle, and end of all beings.
Accurately pairs Vishnu of Adityas, radiant Sun of luminaries, Marici of Maruts, and Moon amid stars.
Directly corresponds to Sama-Veda of Vedas, Vasava (Indra) of devas, and mind among the faculties/senses.
Accurately matches Sankara of Rudras, Vittesha (Kubera) of Yakshas/Rakshasas, Pavaka of Vasus, and Meru of mountain peaks.
Accurately renders Brihaspati among priests, Skanda among heavenly generals, and the Ocean among reservoirs of water.
Matches Bhrigu among great rishis, monosyllable OM among words, Japa-yajna [FN#19] among sacrifices, and Himalayas among immovables.
Accurately enumerates Aswattha among trees, Narada among divine sages, Chitraratha among Gandharvas, and Kapila among Siddhas.
Directly matches Ucchaisravas among steeds born of nectar, Airavata among lordly elephants, and the monarch among men.
Faithfully renders the thunderbolt among weapons, Kamadhuk (Kamadhenu) among cows, and Vasuki among serpent tribes.
Directly maps Ananta among Nagas, Varuna among aquatic deities, Aryam among Pitris, and Yama among dispensers of justice.
Matches Prahlada among Daityas, Time among measures/reckoners, the lordly beast (lion/tiger) among quadrupeds, and Garuda among birds.
Accurately corresponds to wind among purifiers, Rama among armed warriors, Makara among aquatic creatures, and Ganga among rivers.
Renders the beginning, middle, and end of creations, spiritual knowledge among sciences, and constructive speech (vāda) among disputants.
Matches the letter 'A' among characters, the Dvandva compound [FN#20], imperishable Time, and the all-facing Preserver.
Faithfully renders all-devouring Death, origin of future beings, and the seven feminine virtues: fame, fortune, speech, memory, intellect, constancy, and forgiveness.
Accurately identifies Brihatsaman among hymns, Gayatri among metres, Margasirsha among months, and flowering Spring among seasons.
Directly matches the dice game of the deceitful, brilliance of the splendid, victory, resolve/action, and virtue of the good.
Accurately represents Vasudeva among Vrishnis, Arjuna among Pandavas, Vyasa among Munis, and Usanas among poets.
Faithfully renders the rod/sceptre of rulers, statesmanship of victors, silence of secrets, and wisdom of knowers.
Captures the Lord as the generative seed of all beings, without which no moving or unmoving creature can exist.
Directly matches that there is no end to divine vibhūtis, this extensive list being merely an illustrative summary.
Faithfully reflects that whatever is glorious, prosperous, or mighty proceeds from a fragment of the Lord's divine splendour.
Accurately renders the climactic conclusion: supporting and pervading the entire cosmos with a single fraction of His being.

chapterFindings: Chapter 10 contains 42 canonical references; verses 10.4 and 10.5 form a verified shared two-verse span where Arnold combines their list of mental dispositions and attributes into an 8-line rhymed catalogue.
The source footnote marker anomaly [FN#l6] (using lowercase 'l' for digit 1) is faithfully preserved at verse 10.1 without affecting the text integrity.
The heptameter rhyming couplets adopted by Arnold from verse 10.1 onwards adhere closely to the semantic progression of the Sanskrit vibhūti enumerations.
